answer_text:
Interpreting the intended expression as the usual exponential-series remainder

\[
L_n=(n+1)!\left(e-\sum_{k=0}^n \frac1{k!}\right),
\]

we use

\[
e=\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\frac1{k!}.
\]

Then

\[
e-\sum_{k=0}^n \frac1{k!}
=\sum_{k=n+1}^{\infty}\frac1{k!}.
\]

So

\[
L_n=(n+1)!\sum_{k=n+1}^{\infty}\frac1{k!}
=\sum_{k=n+1}^{\infty}\frac{(n+1)!}{k!}.
\]

Write \(k=n+1+m\), \(m\ge 0\). Then

\[
L_n
=1+\sum_{m=1}^{\infty}\frac1{(n+2)(n+3)\cdots(n+m+1)}.
\]

For \(m\ge1\),

\[
(n+2)(n+3)\cdots(n+m+1)\ge (n+2)^m,
\]

so

\[
0\le L_n-1
\le \sum_{m=1}^{\infty}\frac1{(n+2)^m}
=\frac1{n+1}.
\]

Since \(\frac1{n+1}\to 0\), the squeeze theorem gives

\[
\boxed{1}.
\]
